# Japan (JPN) - English-learning market dossier

**Scope:** AI-first spoken-English product with optional teacher escalation. This is a route hypothesis, not a market-size forecast.

## Screening assessment

| Dimension | Score |
| --- | ---: |
| demand | 9 / 10 |
| paid conversion | 10 / 10 |
| delivery | 10 / 10 |
| distribution | 9 / 10 |
| whitespace | 2 / 10 |
| feasibility | 7 / 10 |
| evidence confidence | 8 / 10 |

Scores are analyst assessments. Evidence confidence is separate from attractiveness.

## Commercial reality

- **Likely payer:** Enterprise L&D and motivated professionals; high ability to pay.
- **Most testable outcome:** AI/global-team work and hiring English sold through local enterprise partners.
- **Existing/substitute supply:** Dense test-prep, corporate English, teacher and AI product market.
- **Main risk:** High CAC, deep Japanese localisation and entrenched competitors.
- **Evidence signal:** ETS HR-leader survey: 96% say English importance has increased; survey not national prevalence.

- Begin validation in: Japanese. This is a product-design assumption, not a measure of English demand. Test code-switching, speech recognition, payment preferences and trust language with local users.
- Do not use the EF EPI score (446 in 2025, -8 vs 2024) as a national fluency or willingness-to-pay estimate. The EPI sample is self-selected online test takers.

1. Recruit one employer, college, training centre or other payer matching the stated target outcome.
2. Offer a role-specific 4-6 week speaking path in the local onboarding language.
3. Capture baseline and endline roleplay/assessment; instrument activation, D7/D30 retention, paid conversion, AI minutes, support and any human escalation.
